speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It also demonstrated how Government agencies can work with industry partners to adopt pro-business approaches without affecting regulatory objectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Second, we will cut red tape and simplify our licensing regime to reduce compliance costs for businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The Pro-Enterprise Panel (PEP) is currently working with the Association of Catering Professionals Singapore to do a deep dive into the regulatory requirements for the food sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The food industry is not the biggest sector in our economy, but we chose to start with this as a pilot because we believe the regulatory improvements can benefit many of our SMEs and workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We asked ourselves, is it really necessary to have 14 touchpoints?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I do not know if this pilot will succeed but we will try.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As Minister Ong Ye Kung advised us when we embarked on the review, “Think big, start small, act fast.” We will begin with this pilot, learn from the experience and extend the concept to other sectors subsequently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I believe these moves can have a positive impact on businesses by reducing regulatory costs and speeding up the application processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They also help to shape a more positive pro-enterprise culture amongst our Government agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Third, we will encourage experimentation via mechanisms, such as regulatory sandboxes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This encourages stakeholders to experiment within a well-defined “safe” space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Other agencies like the Ministry of Health and Energy Market Authority have also started their own regulatory sandboxes for telemedicine and the energy sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: There is some risk when we embark on rules review and implement regulatory sandboxes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Some of the pilots could fail and some of the new rules may not work well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: But we have to try, as remaining status quo and playing it safe is simply not tenable when we have to compete with other cities in the world for ideas, investments and talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In such an environment, the most dangerous strategy is to make no bold moves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: What is important is to learn from the failure and have the resilience to bounce back and try again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Being pro-business in our rules is much more than the economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It is about shaping our social norms and our social compact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It is about supporting risk-taking and overcoming our fear of failure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In the process of trying something new, we learn and become more resilient and more resourceful.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Such changes can have a significant and lasting impact on our societal culture and the kind of society we want Singapore to be.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Recently, I met the three Singaporean students who started Binjai Brew – Rahul, Abilash and Heetesh.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They are engineering students at the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and spent a year together at UC Berkeley for their overseas attachment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Rahul did an internship with a brewery in Richmond, California, and that was when they picked up the interest and knowledge to brew their own beer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The three young men experimented with different brewing techniques.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They adopted an engineering approach, building their own fridge to control the temperature settings, measuring the results of different recipes and brewing methods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: After some months of trial and error, they produced good quality beer which they then shared with their friends at NTU, not just one variety but seven different types of beer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I have tried their beer; it is very good.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Unfortunately, they were not able to continue with their brewing on campus.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The students told me that NTU has been very supportive and encouraging and offered to help them to continue while complying with the law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Again, I do not know if we can successfully implement this regulatory change but we will give it a shot.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I told Rahul, Abilash and Heetesh that I admire their enterprising spirit, their willingness to take risks and try something different and their dedication in applying their engineering training to perfect the recipes and brewing techniques.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These attributes will be valuable for them in future, whichever career path they choose.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I hope more of our young people can have similar opportunities to pursue their passion and have support from their families and society to take a less trodden path.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Next, we must believe in our enterprises and our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Singapore companies and workers can compete with the very best in the world and come out on top.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To thrive and grow, Singapore companies know they have to sell to the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To develop products and services for the rest of the world, they have to prove their viability in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We must give them the opportunities and help them to succeed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: All 100,000 trackers were taken up by our enthusiastic participants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Activate built on this success to spin off another company, Actxa, to venture into the wearables industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Actxa is now able to hold a place in the wearables market among well-entrenched competitors, such as Apple and Garmin, and it is developing new innovative products and expanding into overseas markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We have many good local companies run by talented Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: He is the founder and CEO of Riverwood, a home-grown logistics company.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Syafiq dropped out of school when he young as he had to support his family.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: While working as a personal trainer, he picked up useful business lessons and ideas from his clients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: He then started Riverwood, armed with only two vans and four employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Through hard work, taking calculated risks and learning from initial mistakes, Syafiq has grown his company to where it is today, with more than 60 vehicles and over 100 workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: More than 80% of his employees are Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Syafiq also impressed me with his drive to constantly innovate and grow his business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Riverwood has applied technology and productivity measures extensively to boost its competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Syafiq is now looking at supplying halal food products to Japan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I asked him why Japan, the country does not have a large Muslim population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: He explained that the Japanese are interested in halal food products to serve the growing market of Muslim tourists and also to prepare for Tokyo Olympics in 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, there is an opportunity for a company like Riverwood to enter the market and apply their logistics capabilities and the trusted Singapore brand name to ensure process integrity and quality assurance for halal food products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Third, we must have the best talent in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These include training and skills-upgrading for our workers under programmes, such as SkillsFuture, Professional Conversion Programme and Adapt and Grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We also implemented the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) and the Tripartite Standard on the Employment of Term Contract Employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Companies with unfair hiring practices know they will run into problems and troubles with the authorities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And it is certainly not about building walls and closing our doors to new immigrants and global talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With Singapore’s ageing population, such an approach will only hurt the country and our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Singapore produces many talented people through our world-class education system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Singaporeans are held in high regard for our work ethic and reliability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our workers are highly skilled and trustworthy and we have the ability to work in a diverse environment with people from different cultures and backgrounds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The made-in-Singapore Dyson motor is a good example of how our people are collaborating with the best talent in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Dyson, a British company which manufactures household appliances like vacuum cleaners, uses its advanced manufacturing facility in Singapore to produce almost all the digital motors for their appliances sold throughout the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Yvonne Tan, who is Dyson’s research and development engineering manager, has overseen the production of more than 20 million digital motors since joining the company in 2015.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We also have Singaporeans holding senior positions in our multinational corporations (MNCs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Linus Lee heads Twitter’s data science team in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Clarence Chew led Decathlon’s entry into Southeast Asia and Australia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Interacting with our students gives me confidence that our society and our education system have produced many young people with the resilience, resourcefulness and gumption to compete with the best in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I recently attended the graduation ceremony at Ngee Ann Polytechnic (NP) where I met Emmett Goh and Lynette Lau.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Emmett did well at ITE and earned a place at NP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: He won the Tay Eng Soon Gold Medal at the recent graduation ceremony.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: But it was not all rosy for him from the start.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: He was once arrested for getting into a fight with schoolmates when he was 16.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: After that incident, he decided to turn his life around.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: During his time at NP, he did a six-month internship at Metta Nairobi, an entrepreneur’s club that brings startup communities together in Kenya.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Emmett has many dreams he wants to pursue, including joining a private equity firm, running an exotic resort and becoming an inspirational speaker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: During her time with NP, she did a six-month internship with Grab Indonesia where she travelled across 10 cities to conduct market research for its business expansion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: She successfully devised a new method to reduce the backlog of driver sign-ups and increase their productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: She even picked up Bahasa Indonesia during her internship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Lynette is now running a startup, Pixcels, which provides photobook services and she aspires to own a successful business one day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We cannot rely on MNCs alone to achieve this, but neither should we look inward and only focus on local SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I agree with Mr Liang Eng Hwa that the two need to go hand in hand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MNCs benefit from a strong base of SMEs and SMEs can grow and build new capabilities by working with MNCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We need an economy with strong companies, whether they are local offices of MNCs, large local enterprises or SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Ministers Chan Chun Sing and Heng Swee Keat have spoken about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It is not just about growing our economic capital, but also our intellectual capital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is why Silicon Valley remains the "centre of the tech universe".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Nearly three-quarters of its skilled workers are foreign born.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: More than 40% of US companies in the 2017 Fortune 500 list were founded by someone who is foreign-born or has parents who are immigrants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Similarly, many of our startups in Singapore have co-founders who are foreign-born.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Some have now become Singaporeans, adding to Team Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Besides bringing talent into Singapore, we should also think of ways to tap on the large talent pool in our region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We want to grow a group of regional talent who are familiar with Singapore and whom our companies can work with, both in Singapore and when they expand overseas, not only bringing the region into Singapore but also bringing Singapore into the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Enhancing such connectivity will provide more win-win opportunities and help our companies to succeed when they expand overseas, when they operate in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Ultimately, what we want is to strengthen Singapore to benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In a recent Straits Times article, Maybank Kim Eng economist Dr Chua Hak Bin said while there should not be a relaxation of the foreign worker policy across the board, there is a need to look at certain sectors which require talent from abroad to support their growth and allow Singapore to seize opportunities and be at the forefront of change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Dr Chua is right, we cannot compete with other top-tier cities in the premier league if we do not have the best talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Ravi Menon, Managing Director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, has framed the issue very well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: He said: "It is about growing the Singaporean talent base as well as being a magnet for the world's talents...Most of all, being open in spirit and mindset, staying open to diversity, being comfortable working in multicultural settings, thriving in a globalised world, having an enterprising spirit, always seeking new and better ways to do things." I agree with Ravi that this is how we can create more opportunities for our people, to grow our economy, to enable our companies and our workers to do well and to create a better future for our next generation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Thomas Chua feels that the Government and businesses should have trust in each other and learn from each other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This can help the Government to better understand the needs of businesses and help them to succeed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Only by doing well can businesses provide good jobs for workers, support lifelong learning and skills upgrading.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Before entering politics, I had met Mr Thomas Chua several times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I have learnt many things from him, including his views and experience in running his business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I remember that when he was the President of SCCCI, we worked together to set up the Trade Association Hub (TAC Hub) in Jurong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is an important collaboration project between the Government and the Trade Associations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The purpose is to support the development of TACs, deepen the cooperation between the Government and businesses and create a pro-business, pro-worker environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Government agencies must understand the cost impact on SMEs as a result of regulations, listen to their feedback and reduce unnecessary rules and regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With flexible management, we can help businesses to innovate and transform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These enabled Singapore to move from Third World to First in one generation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These changes spurred our local corporations to become more productive and more competitive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Entities like PSA, Singtel and DBS are now leading companies in Asia and have created wealth, good jobs and career development opportunities for many Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And there is room for them to grow further by tapping on the rise of Asia over the next decade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are now in a world where some countries are starting to turn inwards and become more xenophobic and less welcoming to trade and foreign investments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Let us have the courage to once again take a contrarian position by keeping Singapore open and connected with the world and to boldly experiment with innovative ideas and transform our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We must continue to grow, so that we have the resources to hold our society together to invest in our people and build new infrastructure and capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To achieve these goals, we need to be pro-business and pro-worker and ensure that the fruits of economic growth can benefit all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: During his 60th birthday dinner in 1983, Mr Lee Kuan Yew said, "The past 24 years were not pre-ordained.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: There will be unexpected problems ahead, as there were in the past.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They have to be met, grappled with and resolved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education and Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For only a people who are willing to face up to their problems and are prepared to work with their leaders to meet unexpected hardships with courage and resolution, deserve to thrive and to prosper."  Mr Lee's words are a useful reminder for all of us, including a new generation of Singaporeans, to look ahead with confidence as we write the next chapter of the Singapore Story, facing the future together with the same pioneering spirit as our lion-hearted forefathers who built this land.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Please allow me to return to the theme that I have focused on in the last few years and, at the risk of repeating this ad nauseam, housing was, is and remains the key pillar of our social compact with Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Therefore, in our pursuit of a world-class city, one that is well-connected and admired, we cannot forsake the fundamentals.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our development in the last 50 years has been to place the survival of Singapore and the benefit to Singaporeans at the core.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This we must not forsake in our next lap.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I welcome MND's Addendum to Mdm President's speech, especially the reiteration that home ownership gives Singaporeans a tangible stake in our country and a critical sense of belonging.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, I wish to jump in immediately to address a hot potato that has resurfaced in recent months, especially in media opinion pieces.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And this is the issue of 99-year leases.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While it arose because of the collective sale fever at the tail end of last year, I think we should take the opportunity to address this issue now and head on.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The furore that has surrounded it reflects how much home ownership has become part of the Singaporean identity.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The passions that have heated up around its discussion recently are not so much a reflection of angst but perhaps of genuine worry on the ground about how lease decay might fundamentally change the way we view our assets.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For a long time, Singaporeans have known that leases will run down eventually.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is also not that a majority of flats will be reaching the end of their lifespan anytime soon.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In the context of the recent collective sale bubble, lease decay has also led to the unfortunate comparison of parity – that a 20-year-old apartment or a 40-year-old HUDC project can undergo collective sale and thus monetise the asset for the owners and turn back the clock for developers, seems somewhat unfair.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Of course, there are major differences between both.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But, in situations like these, no amount of rational explanation can address the perceived unfairness completely.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What was perhaps a non-issue just not so long ago, has made a number of Singaporeans unduly worried.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One homeowner I met recently shared how she was worried about not being able to sell the family flat in the future.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: All of a sudden, in response to media articles, the family is now making actual plans to sell their 30-plus-year-old flat to purchase a newer one.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Just yesterday, during my block visit, I caught up with two families.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One was worried that their flat value will decline rapidly soon.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Another mother told me that she was contemplating applying for the new projects in Tengah in view of her children growing up.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Given their worries, you would be forgiven for thinking that this block I visited is quite old.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In fact, it is all of only 21 years old.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, this reaction to this decay has perhaps taken on a life of its own.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Ultimately, we all know that housing is, fundamentally, a depreciating asset in the long run.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But with such widespread concern, I think some clarity from the Ministry and the Government is called for at this point in time.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Because we cannot, on the one hand, say that home ownership offers a tangible stake but, at the same time, have homeowners wondering how stable and lasting that stake will be for them.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Let us take this from the view that we are a land-scarce city state.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Even the recent projects that we have announced means that we take over land from areas set aside for other developments in the past like in Tengah, Paya Lebar, an airbase, and Bidadari, a former cemetery, for housing development.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Those of us who look after Town Councils can attest to that.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Constant piecemeal upgrading might not be the most cost-efficient method beyond a certain age.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Last year, Premier Li Keqiang, announced that the government of China would be seriously considering a Real-estate Protection Provision, a change in the law to automatically renew the leases, but because it is such a complex issue, they have set up a committee to review this over three years.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For us in Singapore, we are still some way from that magical age.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But it does not hurt to consider long-term solutions now and reassure Singaporeans of their stake in the country.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have seen one example of early success with the completion of Kampung Admiralty.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While retirement communities are one way forward, I urge the Government to also put serious consideration into helping more elders age inplace.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My constituency of Yew Tee is an upgraders' town, which means that many of our residents moved in in their late 30s and early 40s just about two decades ago.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These are their second flats, upgraded from their first matrimonial homes.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: After 20 years, these first generation of owners have aged as our town has matured.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They look at their 4-room neighbours and ask why the Government will not extend the Lease-Buyback Scheme (LBS) to them.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Government has already revised the flat sizes once before, they say.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Attachment to a place gives a greater sense of belonging, especially to older Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is a place that they are familiar with, comfortable with.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As more of these naturally occurring retirement communities are formed, early identification of demographic shifts will allow the Government to plan ahead to put in place resources and facilities to cater for the needs of our elders.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: From my visit to older residents, some areas to consider include suggestions of lower wash areas, kitchen tops for elders dependent on mobility aids or wheelchairs.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Like other hon Members, I also believe that technology will play a big part in our next lap.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Beyond the grab-bars, ramps and accessibility ramps connecting our elders to the wider world through technology should also be explored.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Items, such as home monitoring systems, home alarms, elements that allow the home itself to take care of you, preparing communal facilities in advance are also an important step.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Let us take my constituency again as an example.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Yew Tee is usually regarded as a relatively young town by our total population.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, when I made the decision to convert one of our early childhood education centres to a senior care centre a number of years ago, I was asked why.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But as I had alluded to earlier, though we are statistically quite young, the transition to the silver years will occur in bulk once the first generation of home owners enters their late 50s and 60s.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Today, our Senior Care Centre is already up and running and almost at full capacity.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, if we had waited till the demographics changed, we would have had to play catch-up.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Over the last few years, I have also been urging the Government to do more for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am, therefore, heartened that MND has made significant changes to address the housing needs of our singles, including single parents and divorcees.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Certain additional conditions contingent on employment and income can also be factored in.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This will allow those who are lower- to lower-medium income earners who are singles to obtain a flat which might be out of reach for them on a single-income based on the longer leases.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have encountered enough examples of singles, especially divorcees, who face sometimes unsurmountable barriers to their next housing option.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Extending this additional option to them and other singles will, similarly, give them an opportunity to have a continued stake in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: (In Mandarin):   This is a poem that was written by a famous poet Du Fu from the Tang Dynasty and the title is “The song of my thatched cottage being destroyed by the autumn wind”.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It demonstrated his concern for the country and people.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To explain in modern language, the poet asked himself in the poem that, when the thatch on his cottage roof had been blown away, “How can we provide thousands of big and bright houses to house all the poor in the country so that they can live happily?” The houses will not be shaken by rain and wind, as steady as a mountain.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mr Pan Shou, our famous local calligrapher, has written this poem, which is now displayed in the foyer of HDB Hub.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This has shown the commitment and the resolve of our Government to improve our people’s living environment.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We can say that Singapore has achieved the dream of Du Fu to allow everyone to have a place to live.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The older generation of Singaporeans will be familiar with the housing shortage situation around 1959, which led to social instability.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The PAP Government decided to treat the housing issue as one of its fundamental national policies.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is something which we should be proud of.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We must not forget this in the next phase of our national development.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While we pursue to become a modern and advanced metropolis, we must continue to keep in mind Du Fu’s poem and adopt a people-centric approach by putting people’s interest and welfare at the centre of our development efforts.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In terms of urban planning, I hope the Government will continue to maintain our unique Southeast Asian characteristics and history and promote the development of the unique culture of our various ethnic groups.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As we develop, we must not forget our roots.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We must build a future city which can give the people a sense of belonging and identity.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Only by doing this can we demonstrate that Singapore is not just a modern and advanced city but also an endearing home.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Mdm President, in her Address to this House, said and I quote, "With bold thinking, we will create a metropolis that will embrace the future." This metropolis must, indeed, embrace the future for Singapore to progress.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To the lonely elderly, may this new metropolis bring warmth and the comfort of friendship of care.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To young families, may this metropolis provide opportunities to excel in their work and also to raise a family in a supportive environment.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Only then will this metropolis shine even brighter as a little red dot.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The President mentioned that Singaporeans want to live in a fair and just society.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: She also asked that we must have the courage to go for bold changes and not just tweak things at the margin.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One area which I think we should re-consider is our unwritten principle of relying on market forces and being generally reluctant to impose too much regulation in the spirit of promoting free enterprise.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, market forces may, at times, result in inequitable outcomes.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Upon the expiry of the three-year period, many tenants received a rude shock from these landlords that rates have increased significantly.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They are thus forced to pay the higher rentals.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Even if they choose to move out, they would face heavy losses as their investment in the furniture and fittings would become worthless.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, very often, they even have to fork out more money to reinstate the premises to the original bare shell condition.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The current situation thus allows the landlords to hold small businesses ransom due to the unequal bargaining positions.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Our fellow Member, Mr Murali Pillai, also spoke about this during an Adjournment Motion on the power imbalance in contracts involving small businesses in February this year.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In his speech, he advocated offering small businesses the same level of protection as would be offered to individuals.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is the case in Australia and, to a lesser extent, Hong Kong.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, there is an urgent need to relook how such unfair practices are affecting small businesses.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If left unchecked, it may harm entrepreneurship, increase cost of doing business and, eventually, lead to higher cost of living in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The short lease period would not allow them to build up a steady clientele base for them to recover their investment in their furniture and fittings.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This allows a longer runway for SMEs to build up their businesses and recover their investment in the premises.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will help to lower business cost and discourage landlords from inserting the reinstatement requirement into their leasing contracts.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The reinstatement requirement is not only costly to businesses but also environmentally wasteful.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Without the reinstatement clause, businesses, which take over the furniture and fittings may only need to make minor renovation adjustments.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, for too long, we have left things to market forces and not impose any regulation on commercial and retail leases.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I think it is time to consider this as a sacred cow which we have to slay in the name of fairness and help to level the playing field for small businesses.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: On this note, I reaffirm my support for the Motion.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The President's speech laid out the priorities of the Government and I will focus my remarks today on how we can build a better city, one that is more innovative, inclusive and resilient.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We often think of cities as buildings, hardware and infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But cities can also be thought of as living organisms.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In nature, it is survival of the fittest.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, cities must evolve and adapt to survive in an ever-changing world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is no such thing as status quo; we are either improving or we are declining and going backwards.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And there are countless examples of cities that once were centres of economic activity, but are no longer relevant today.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, many emerging cities are working hard to leap-frog the competition and get to the top.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the choice for Singapore is simple: adapt or perish.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the last 700 years, Singapore's fortune had waxed and waned.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The ancient seaport of Singapura thrived in the late 13th century.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, it was described in the Malay annals as the first great Malay trading port.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But by the 15th century, the port had declined and the city had been depopulated.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then, the arrival of the British in 1819 set Singapore on a different trajectory, which is why we are commemorating the bicentennial next year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Post-Independence, we have succeeded against tough odds and moved from third world to first.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In answering that question, I think we have to also reflect on our fundamental purpose.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And as Mr Gan Thiam Poh said yesterday, Singapore's raison d’etre has been and will continue to be that of a trading hub serving the region and the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in today's world, it is not just about trading in goods.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is also about the flow of people, talent, finance and other services.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is about being at the centre of action, the centre of research, knowledge-based and innovation activities across Asia and the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why, in his Budget speech this year, Minister Heng Swee Keat talked about anchoring Singapore as a Global-Asian node of innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the east, we are reviewing how the entire area around the expanded Changi Airport can be renewed and put to better use.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we can develop new industries, especially those related to the aviation sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And these activities can also benefit from linkages with the nearby Changi Business Park and SUTD.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, in the west, we are looking at new industry clusters that can be located next to the port and leverage on synergies with the port.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These will also be connected to broader developments in the west, including the Jurong Innovation District and Jurong Lake District.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the north, we are stitching together multiple developments, from Woodlands to Sembawang and Seletar, as well as the upcoming Punggol Digital District.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, it is an entire northern corridor, which can anchor new businesses and investments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The point is that we are not just doing more of the same.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Each new development will be better than the one before.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Each new project will push the boundary and pilot innovative solutions to make our city more attractive and further enhance our quality of life.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this is what we have been doing all the while.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Look at what we have done in our HDB towns.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The blueprint was launched in 1996 and then we had to slow down due to the financial crisis.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we improved and upgraded the plan, relaunched it in 2007.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, Punggol it is almost complete and it is a beautiful waterfront town where new flats are very popular with young couples.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The site is bigger than Ang Mo Kio or Bishan.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, there are huge opportunities for further urban innovation for a better quality of life for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the same way, we have been constantly developing and improving our city centre.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We started by renewing our CBD in the 1970s to create more office space.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then, we extended the CBD to Marina Bay.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We started reclaiming the land in the 1970s.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We launched the masterplan for Marina Bay in 1983 and, over the subsequent years and decades, worked hard at conceiving and developing the Marina Bay that we have today.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The space is three times the size of Marina Bay.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we want the impact to be much more than three times of Marina Bay.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is a completely blank canvas for all of us to dream of exciting new possibilities for the future and to make these dreams come true.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, when we say that we are not done building Singapore, it is not a slogan.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a single-minded commitment and mission to keep building and improving our city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I can confidently say that, over the coming years and decades, Singapore will be undergoing its most extensive transformation yet.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To make Singapore one of the great cities of the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A truly outstanding city to live, work and play, the kind that people talk about and return to over and over again.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A city where everyone belongs; where all of us are proud to call home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: An outstanding city is not just economically vibrant but it also needs to be socially inclusive; a place that embraces diversity, where different groups mix easily and have equal opportunities to participate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Unfortunately, if you look around us, it is not always the case in many cities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Often, the downtown area looks good, but other areas in the city are left to deteriorate, resulting in urban slums.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From time to time, you will see segregation of neighbourhoods: between rich and poor; between ethnic groups; between young and old.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have worked very hard to avoid these problems in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every HDB town has a balanced mix of residents across different ethnic groups and backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every town has a mix of public-private developments, as well as different HDB flat types catering to diverse needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every town has common spaces where residents of different backgrounds get together, socialise and forge shared memories together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have playgrounds and fields where the children grow up and play.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And, personally, growing up in Marine Parade, I still have very fond memories of the dragon playground downstairs next to my block and the children from all around that block coming down to play together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of us may not know one another very well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From different backgrounds, it does not matter, we all get together to play.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The void decks used to always be animated with activities; it will be a real treat for us to see a magic show and then there will be potluck and the parents will cook and we all eat together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this special quality of HDB living, I am sure all of you can attest to is still alive and well today.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have done well in the last 50 years, but more still needs to be done.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our housing and urban plans must continue to push back against the growing pressures of inequality and social stratification.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We cannot just leave things to chance, but we must deliberately plan for a more equal and inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why we have been building more rental flats with newer, better designs, alongside the sold flats in various HDB towns.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also doing more to help families in our rental flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is not bad but we must do even better than that.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MND will be working with MSF, SSOs and the VWOs to see how best we can support the families, help them solve their issues holistically and get back on their feet.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides looking out for rental families, we must also take care of the elderly, especially those who are living on their own in studio and 2-room flexi apartments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do not want them to feel isolated and disengaged, as Members have highlighted just now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we are putting a lot more emphasis in the way we design our HDB flats and estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This means more shared public spaces, like civic plazas and community gardens, for them to stay active.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Another aspect of inclusive development is to continually renew our buildings and infrastructure, because we do not want a situation where certain parts of Singapore are left to degrade and we end up with deteriorated neighbourhoods or towns, inhabited largely by lower-income or elderly residents.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It requires the Town Councils to do proper maintenance and upkeeping of the estate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It requires residents to take care of the neighbourhood.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the Government has and will continue to do its part.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All Members are familiar with the programmes we have put in place for estate renewal.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have the Selective En-bloc Redevelopment Scheme (SERS), Remaking our Heartlands (ROH), Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) and Home Improvement Programme (HIP).

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of these programmes are scoped carefully to ensure they are fiscally sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: SERS, as the name implies, is done only on a very selective basis.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: ROH is for town-wide enhancements; we have largely completed six towns and consultations are ongoing for three towns now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: NRP which is for neighbourhood facilities, is ongoing for blocks built up to 1995.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And HIP for enhancements or for retrofitting within the unit itself, is being completed for the flats that were built up to 1986.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The selection of flats will be done as soon as possible so that we can complete this batch of HIP.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Members have asked for extensions of these programmes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You would like to know when ROH can be done for your town; or when HIP can be extended to the newer flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do want to renew and rejuvenate our HDB towns in an orderly fashion.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But as I have explained before, upgrading projects are expensive and span many years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we are studying this carefully to make sure that we have the resources to follow through on any future commitments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ninety-nine years is a long time – it covers two generations.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The oldest HDB flat today is around 50 years and the vast majority have more than 60 years remaining.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this is not an immediate issue at all.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Yet, some have already called for automatic lease extensions or for HDB lease top-ups by private developers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will be easy for me to give you a politically expedient answer now and try to wave away the problem.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there are serious trade-offs and ramifications to consider.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It sounds easy to do but it is not a straightforward matter.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, we should not assume everyone wants it.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, as all of us who run Town Councils know, much more maintenance is needed for older flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Imagine the flat beyond 99 years and how much more maintenance is needed and how costly it will be for residents.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More importantly, despite our best efforts at planning, we are still severely constrained by space in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If there is no more land to recycle for future public housing, then what will happen to our children and grandchildren?

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: How will they have access to subsidised housing in the future?

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this is a complex issue and I am glad many Members who spoke about this recognise this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members have offered suggestions, including Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Alex Yam.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Leon Perera also spoke about this and I look forward to the Workers' Party's suggestions on this matter because he said that the Workers' Party is studying this matter very seriously and I look forward to receiving your suggestions as well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, we welcome views on this matter from all parties and all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise that it is a matter that Singaporeans care about and we want to listen to your views and feedback.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, the Government must grapple with these difficult questions, study the matter and do the responsible thing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our duty is not just to the current generation who already own homes, but also to the future generations – those not yet voting and those not yet born, those whose lives and future depend on us making the right decisions now, on their behalf.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the end of the day, we want to ensure that every generation will be able to have an affordable and quality home in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We still have the time to do this work, as I have emphasised earlier but, for now, what is important is that we do not speculate, we do not spread misinformation which can impact the market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, recently there was speculation that the Government would stop the use of CPF entirely for the purchase of HDB flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It started from a media report highlighting a suggestion from an academic.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He later clarified that the article did not fully reflect his views, yet, the information continued to circulate online and through WhatsApp groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even for older flats, CPF can still be used but under certain conditions to safeguard retirement adequacy of home-buyers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There has also been concern about the impact of lease expiry on HDB prices.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there is still value in older HDB flats – value which can be unlocked for retirement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We looked at real transaction data over the past year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, a 4-room flat with less than 60 years remaining can sell for more than $600,000; a 5-room flat can sell for more than $800,000.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Not pretend data, theoretical data; transaction data over the past year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the transacted price depends not just on length of remaining lease, clearly, but it also depends on many other attributes – factors like location, the storey height, the condition of the flat, these are all very relevant.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Whatever the price you get from the sale of a flat today, the sales proceeds would be more than sufficient to purchase a smaller flat for retirement, for those who are interested in right-sizing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I give you an actual example that happened recently.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Abdul Aziz Haji Hamdan, who is 67 years old, originally owned a 3-room flat in Marsiling with around 60 years of lease remaining.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He decided to right-size to a Studio Apartment in Kampung Admiralty with a 30-year lease.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He sold his 3-room flat for $250,000, purchased the Studio Apartment for just over $100,000.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, he has more than $140,000 in cash and CPF proceeds to supplement his retirement savings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Buying and selling a property can be a complex undertaking and it is easy to get carried away by market sentiments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Just not too long ago, there were people speculating in older HDB flats hoping to get SERS benefits and not explicitly saying that they were doing that.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, the reverse has happened and there are people overly anxious about how much their older flats can fetch in the resale market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, my advice to Singaporeans is this: do not buy or sell based on speculative information.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Look at the facts and, if you are in the market for a home, do your homework carefully and choose something that fits your needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will make the resale market work better for potential buyers and sellers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, I was reminded of this in a recent MPS.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One resident came to me to seek help for more time to sell their flat because they could not get the price that they were looking for.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Right after that, another resident came and said, "I need a flat urgently, please give me a direct allocation of a flat from HDB".

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I told her, "I can't do that, you got to ballot, but if you want your flat so urgently, why don't you go to the resale market?" And she immediately said, "Resale market too expensive." So, on the one hand, sellers find it hard to sell; on the other hand, buyers are saying that prices are still too high.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides the public housing market, we are also watching the private housing market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The property market, like any other asset market, will go through ups and downs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But neither do we take a completely hands-off approach.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise that there may be over-borrowing in a very low interest rate environment and that sharp price changes that run ahead of fundamentals can be destabilising to the broader economy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, it is understandable why housing remains a top concern for all our people.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: My assurance is that the Government will continue to provide affordable and quality homes for all Singaporeans – both now and into the future.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will make sure that, in every town, we have a range of housing and amenities for all ages; more shared spaces for all to enjoy; and a place where every Singaporean feels that they belong.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides being more innovative and inclusive, we also have to incorporate resilience in our urban development.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What will happen to the world in the next 50 years?

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we can be sure there will always be crises and threats and even black swan events.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we have to build resilience into our city and urban systems.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One big unknown is whether the planet can continue to sustain continued economic activities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If the world does not do enough to tackle climate change, Singapore will be at risk of coastal inundation due to sea level rises.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we need to start making preparations now to strengthen Singapore’s resilience against climate change.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The dike system in the polder is designed to cater for sea-level rise and the dike can be raised and upgraded more easily compared to traditional reclamation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Concurrently, we are also studying how best to safeguard Singapore’s long-term coastal protection needs and we are undertaking detailed modelling and engineering studies for this purpose so that we can identify and recommend appropriate protection strategies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They may include use of dikes, pumps or other technologies, but the most important thing is to be prepared.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this is just one example of how we are building resilience into our system and there are many more things that we will need to do to be a more resilient city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The urban transformation plans I have shared are significant in scale and require considerable fiscal resources.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Pritam Singh said earlier in the Debate that the current Government has more financial resources than previous generations of PAP leaders.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But he forgot to mention that our fiscal commitments and spending are also at their highest ever levels.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singaporeans today are being provided with more services and support than before.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For now, we are just able to meet all of our spending needs with current resources.

speaker: The Minister for National Development and Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
