text: But to my resident whose dignity had been hurt, what is a fair and just society?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are all born with a sense of dignity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some describe dignity as a sense of being valued, a feeling of being respected, a sensation of esteem of self-worth.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is tied to our self-identity, to the things that matter to us, and it is reinforced daily on how others react to us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When our dignity is maintained and our self-worth reinforced through words or deeds, we are at peace with ourselves and with society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When our dignity is threatened and our self-worth questioned, we may react in anger against those who look down on us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I would say, that how we recognise one another's needs for dignity and protect it, has implications for how fair and just our society is perceived to be and for social harmony.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To achieve a sense of fairness and justness, Government policies which preserve meritocracy, equality and promote self-help are important.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To a large extent, our Government policies strive to create equality in our society by making sure that all citizens have access to education, medical care, basic home ownership and jobs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This allows everyone to have the basics to live a life with dignity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And even for those who drop out or have fallen behind, there are Government schemes to provide them an opportunity to get back on again.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And should new gaps appear in society, Government policies will be looked at again to deal with new issues and new inequalities which may come about.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But apart from good policies which strive to create equality, we should also be mindful of the processes and social interactions which can affect an individual's sense of dignity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, when the vulnerable and the needy go to Government agencies for help, are our processes sensitive to their needs?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Do we make them feel that they are valued citizens, albeit they need help at this juncture?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Are we mindful of the constraints that they face?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I believe that every time a citizen comes forward to seek help, it is a moment in his life where we could help effect change.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A moment where we could try to right life's inequalities, a moment where we could make an individual feel that he is respected and valued, regardless of his station in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I may never know the exact details of his original encounter.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This episode taught me that in our interactions with our fellow men, we need to put ourselves in their shoes, speak the language they speak, consider the options put to them to their world view.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Sometimes, it is not so much what we do, but how we do it that matters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But creating an environment where people feel that they are respected and their sense of dignity is upheld, is not just the role of the Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That they become ways to pigeonhole or exclude others knowingly or unknowingly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is where each of us can play a role, that we not become a perpetrator of such social markers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Instead, we should treat those around us, our fellow men, with mutual respect and compassion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is only when mutual respect becomes part of our bigger culture that we can be assured that every citizen feels valued and respected just being part of our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, in our everyday interactions when we come across a service staff, a cleaner, a waiter, do we acknowledge their presence, smile at them and thank them for their work?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When we walk into a shop, are we considerate to the shop assistants?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is genuine respect for someone else's work and consideration for someone else's dignity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And to our young, do we show them through our words and our actions that we value them regardless of what school they go to, how well they do in school and that we respect them as multi-dimensional individuals with various different potentials?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When we have compassion and mutual respect for our fellow men and we demonstrate it through our words and our deeds, we uphold their dignity and we make a statement about what we hold dear in our society, that regardless of what life has in store for individuals and its infinitely varied and unequal economic outcomes, everyone has a place in Singapore society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When we respect one another and treat one another with civility and dignity, this mutuality of respect becomes a powerful anchoring force, providing assurance to every individual that he is loved and accepted.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This brings people close together because they know that they are accepted, come what may.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And this is the antithesis to social markers which serve to divide and to differentiate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There will be new winners and new losers in a new paradigm.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Amidst this tidal wave of change, individuals will be seeking new anchors to preserve their world view and their sense of self-worth as jobs are disrupted and skills have to be relearnt.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: How we manage this transition together and how we help others around us will be a true mark of our compassion for our fellow men and our resilience as a nation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):  : Mr Speaker, recently at my Meet-the-People session, a resident, Mr Wong, came to see me.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He said he had an unhappy experience not too long ago when applying for a certain licence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He said that because he could not speak English, the staff at the counter could not understand him and asked him to stand aside.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The staff then started to serve other residents and later tried to talk him into leaving.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Wong recounted his encounter over and over and could not get over it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He felt that the staff looked down on him.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He also felt that people around him also started to look down on him after knowing that he could not speak English.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Although I could not verify what exactly was the attitude of the staff at that time, according to Mr Wong, the expression and the look of the people around him have hurt his dignity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some say dignity is a sense of being respected and valued.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is the indication of self-esteem and self-worthiness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In this society, only when the dignity of each person is protected can people feel a sense of belonging and the whole society be cohesive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the juncture of this new era, it is even more important to protect the dignity of individuals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Amidst this tidal wave of change, many professions will be disrupted and new winners and losers will emerge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At this time, Singaporeans will need psychological and spiritual anchors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When faced with failure and humiliation, can we still maintain an optimistic and a positive mindset?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Can we still maintain our confidence and courage?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I think this will require our society to be more inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the past few days, Ministers and Members of Parliament talked about social inequality.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To solve the issue of inequality, for sure, Government policies will play a role.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, we also need to realise that inequality is usually a perception.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Even if we have the right policy, if we do not respect one another, people will not feel real equality.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In fact, his application was a rather simple process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Sometimes, certain words we utter and certain body language could affect others profoundly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He may feel that his dignity is hurt and the society is unfair to him.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When communicating and interacting with residents, if we could pay attention to details and be sensitive to one another's needs, unnecessary misunderstandings could be avoided.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Each time we meet a resident, it provides us a valuable opportunity to help him, an opportunity to correct his perception of imbalances in life, and even an opportunity to change his life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Hence, we should treasure each opportunity when we meet the residents and make an effort to attend to the details, so that they truly feel that Singapore is a country with a human touch.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Meanwhile, if each of us, regardless of race, religion and language, can have enough cultural confidence and leave some space for one another, then we will be able to feel that this is an equal and inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My speech will focus on forging a strong national identity through four key areas.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, virtual world to real world; second, volunteerism/community involvement; third, sense of belonging; fourth, foreign policy.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We are today moving into an era where many things we see and do are unthinkable just a decade ago.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We are in the age of disruptive technology.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: People can sit at home and let their fingers do the walking and talking.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But we can turn these technological tools to our advantage.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We often talk about the disappearing kampung spirit.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, this kampung spirit has moved to the virtual world.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They take a different form, that is all.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There are so many kampungs in our Whatsapp and Facebook chat groups.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some chats have groups with as many as 50 to 60 people, or as few as 10 or less.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These private app chats are today’s mini kampungs where people communicate, share opinions, comments, news, videos and so on.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I would call this the era of GenApps, a time when what is unthinkable today can be tomorrow’s reality.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But to forge a strong Singapore identity, groups in the virtual world should move to the real world.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To all chat groups, I make this call to not just stay in the virtual world.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Please come forward and join our community when we celebrate our National Day and other festive celebrations.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: At such events and at subsequent events, we meet one another, get to know one another better, share our common interests and forge deep bonds.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Because of this relationship, we share joys and, should a crisis arise, you and I, our actions and reactions, our response to the call for help, would be more robust.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Another platform that we can promote and forge a common identity is through volunteerism.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I urge everyone, whether you are in school, a youth, a working adult or a retiree, we can all make our contributions.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The energy and the commitment you bring will no doubt improve many lives.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We derive deep satisfaction through meaningful interactions, build up our circle of friends, join in the various activities and build up a sense of belonging to the community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: People who volunteer together, play together and participate in activities together will build interpersonal relationships, trust and attachment to one another.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our Government has done much to invest in the physical infrastructure for our community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As a community, we can do even more to benefit our people in building and strengthening heartware.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We can provide the emotional support to bring our people together.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This helps us to address gaps, duplication, so that limited resources can be spread to more beneficiaries and holistic help can be provided and urgent cases attended to quickly.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Thus, instead of each organisation working in silos, we work together.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Instead of solely depending on the Government to help, the community is involved.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition, we provide a platform for our beneficiaries to volunteer, as this gives them a sense of pride and dignity where they are also contributing to the community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Speaking of pride and dignity, the Government can do well to offer our seniors career opportunities, especially the female workforce.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is an area where we can tap on our readily available workforce.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There is a growing pool of retirees whom we should look to rely on as a good source to meet our skilled manpower needs.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many of our retirees are healthy, well-educated, well-informed and with good work ethos.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can they not have a second career opportunity to pursue their dreams?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I had shared this anecdote in the Budget Debate.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But a good story is one that deserves to be retold.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One of my residents, Mdm Maureen Tan, aged 69, living in Strathmore Avenue used to work as a personal assistant in a bank.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: At the same time, she had always cared for her grandchildren and even helped to babysit her neighbours’ children whenever she had the time.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: After her retirement, she became a full-time caregiver to her two grandchildren.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Her neighbours knew she doted on children and would occasionally ask her to babysit for them when they had errands to run.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Last year, Maureen approached the Henderson Dawson PAP Community Foundation (PCF) Sparkletots Childcare Centre and volunteered her services.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As the teachers saw she had so much love for the children, the centre offered her a job.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: She now interacts with the children, keeps them comfortable and showers them with all her tender love and care.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: At 69, she is healthy, experienced and very committed.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: She sees her work with PCF as a second career.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: She will be very happy if she can be offered a career path, so that she can develop herself.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I believe the Government can offer retirees like Mdm Maureen Tan a second career and develop a career path for them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In doing so, we give our seniors a sense of belonging and participation in the new chapters of the Singapore story.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Another area where we can strengthen our identity is to help educate our people on the many things that our leaders are doing in the field of foreign policy.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We need to explain in simple terms the areas that our Government is doing in foreign affairs which are often not understood by the man-in-the-street.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The current Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) website offers information but on very few subjects and it is more event-based.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The ASEAN page gives some exposure to the grouping, but it is still very limited to the history and the deliberations and events.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This, I feel, can help our people forge an even stronger Singaporean identity.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):  : Mr Speaker, another area where we can strengthen our identity is to help educate our people on the many things that our leaders are doing in the field of foreign policy.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We need to explain in simple terms the areas that our Government is doing in foreign affairs which are often not understood by the man-in-the-street.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, how decisions at ASEAN summits impact our lives.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Or how our participation in international treaties and agreements, such as FTAs or the Paris Agreement on Climate Change impacts on our lives.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How important is it to be chosen as host to the Trump-Kim Jong-un Summit?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In this information age, I would like to propose to MFA to set up a portal and provide bite-size information on our foreign policies where our people can look up on our stand and understand why certain decisions are made and why certain comments are made.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This can deepen our understanding of our foreign policies and our man-in-the-street can be ambassadors of our foreign policies, too.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This, I feel, can help our people forge an even stronger Singaporean identity.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I look forward to our new leaders working with all Singaporeans to take us to the next level.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Every once in a while, the topic of the Singapore Identity comes up.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Often, it is couched as a question: do we have a defining identity in view of our relatively short history?

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At other times, it is an expression of angst.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We point to kiasuism, competitiveness and stress, and we ask ourselves are these all there is to us?

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are known to be pragmatic, logical and rational but this also prompts us to wonder: “Are we all head and no heart?” When I came to the Chamber just now, I found on my seat a brown envelope from Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She had inserted inside a copy of the letter from the National University of Singapore (NUS) students of Tembusu College to the fourth Prime Minister of Singapore that was widely publicised.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In that letter, the students expressed their concerns, their hopes, their fears, many of those related to the Singapore Identity.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The question of the Singapore Identity is particularly pertinent as we enter a new phase of the Singapore Story.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Politically, we see the rise of China, the introspection of America, new tensions in the Middle East, Britain’s exit from the European Union, and, closer to home, a new situation in Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The global economic centre of gravity is shifting to Asia.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Technology is penetrating lives and changing lifestyles, disrupting old jobs and creating new ones.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is triggering innovation and posing fresh conundrums.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Socially, we and the rest of the world are grappling with income inequality, social stratification and the dangers of polarisation.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our population is ageing; new births are not replacing the ones who pass on; and amidst all these, the ever-present shadow of terrorism.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Against this backdrop, the following questions arise: do we, this generation of Singaporeans, have what it takes to deal with these challenges and come out ahead?

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this time of change, what anchors us?

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Who are we and what do we stand for?

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: What kind of future do we want to make for ourselves?

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: From the 14th century, Singapura emerged as a thriving emporium built on regional trade.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Open trade and commerce have always been in our lifeblood.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore declined in the early 1700s due to the rise and relocation of other economic centres in the region.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is an early lesson on what happens when you are overtaken by competition.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: You lose your relevance and slide into obscurity.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The founding by Raffles in 1819 gave us a new lease of life.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The bold move to make Singapore a free port and an open centre of free trade not only re-established our economic importance, but it took us beyond the region, plugging us into global trade for the very first time.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This global connection has carried on to the present day and continues to shape our economic outlook.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It also led to the coming of many peoples and the establishment of many cultures – the beginnings of our multiculturalism.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over the next 150 years, sojourners became settlers.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We were not yet one people; not yet a nation.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But from a harbour, Singapore was becoming home.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a colony, Singapore grew in economic and strategic importance.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But in the 1940s, the winds of war swept the world and we were not spared.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The year 1941 saw the fall of Singapore, an ignominious blow to the invincibility of the British Empire.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It shattered forever the idea of the inevitability of colonial rule.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Japanese Occupation was a period of subjugation and suffering, sacrifice and bloodshed, experienced directly by our parents and grandparents.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is why, even to this day, the word "Syonan" evokes strong reactions.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With the end of WWII, came a global tide of anti-colonialism and the rise of nation states.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The upswell of a strong nationalist spirit, and a fierce desire for the right to determine our own future.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next came the turbulent years of internal self-government, merger, Separation and, finally, Independence.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In just 24 years, we made the tumultuous transition from subjugation to sovereignty.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Who then are we, the people who have made this journey?

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Well, we are a people with a strong sense of self-determination.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have a deep and abiding belief that our future should be charted, not by others, but by ourselves, and on our own terms.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will preserve and protect that inalienable right.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is why the President’s Address makes securing Singapore’s place in the world one of our priorities.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is also why we do not allow external interference with our politics.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a small country, we are often subject to external pressures.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This takes courage, deftness and a healthy sense of realism.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Long before multiculturalism became a buzzword, we made it part of our identity as a nation.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The power of Mr Lee Kuan Yew's words in 1965 still resonates today, when he said: "We are going to have a multiracial nation in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is not a Malay nation; this is not a Chinese nation; this is not an Indian nation.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Everybody will have his place: equal; language, culture, religion." To be Singaporean is to accept that all can practise their faiths, as long as you do not do harm to others.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To be Singaporean is to be able to have your own distinct racial identity while, at the same time, being part of a larger Singaporean family, and sharing a broader national identity with many other races.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To be Singaporean is to be able to appreciate and celebrate other cultures, while retaining your own.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To be Singaporean is also to be part of a uniquely Singaporean culture: Singlish, eating at hawker centres, the concept of "choping", especially with a packet of tissue paper, our habit of calling everyone Auntie or Uncle, whether or not they are related to us; our preferred dress style – casual wear and slippers.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And when you say "fun shot", every Singaporean immediately knows they must put their thumbs up!

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These are things which cut across all ethnicities.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the core of our Singaporean identity is our values.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Because of our values, our hallmark is trust.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In global and regional trade, many accord a premium to dealing with Singaporean businesses.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Multinational corporations (MNCs) set up shop here and investors invest because they know we can be trusted.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a country and as a people, our brand is trustworthiness, reliability.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When we say we will do something, we will.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our biggest commitment is closely interwoven with our identity.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is to be found in the pledge.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: What is the pledge but a commitment, by every Singaporean to one another, to build a better life together?

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the pledge: we affirm our unity; we define the kind of society we want to build together – democratic, based on justice and equality; we set out our goals – happiness, prosperity and progress for everyone.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is instilled in every Singaporean schoolchild, every adult.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Anyone who becomes a citizen must take that pledge as one of the first acts of citizenship and understand, through the pledge, what it means to be Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The pursuit of excellence is also part of our identity.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is a function of our size and lack of natural resources.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If we want anyone to pay attention to us, if we want to have a place at the international table, if we are to secure our position in the world, then we have to be better than merely good.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And through our combined efforts as a people, we are.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are a tiny island of 719 square kilometres.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have a population of 5.5 million, of which 3.4 million are citizens.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are 193 member states in the United Nations.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Almost all of them are bigger, more populous and far more generously endowed with natural resources than we are.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In 2016, PSA Singapore was ranked Best Container Terminal Asia.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Changi Airport, in 2018, it was voted the World’s Best Airport for the sixth consecutive year.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore Airlines (SIA) is the No 1 airline in the world.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore is the third most preferred seat of arbitration globally.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore is the fourth top financial centre in the world.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In global mobility, the Singapore passport is the most powerful in the world in terms of global mobility.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our water story has been an amazing one.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have taken the little we have and made it robust and sustainable.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore is a world leader in water recycling.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the 2017 benchmarking exercise by the European Benchmarking Co-operation Foundation, the Public Utilities Board (PUB) was ranked in the top 10% of water utilities benchmarked for (a) compliance with applicable standards for drinking water tests, and (b) wastewater treatment plant compliance with discharge standards.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have one of the lowest unaccounted-for-water (UFW) rates in the world.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: PUB received the Stockholm Industry Water Award in 2007 and was named Water Agency of the Year in 2006 for being an exemplary model of integrated water management.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over the years, Singapore has had many child prodigies in music.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The most recent is 11-year-old violinist Chloe Chua, who won first prize in the junior division of the Menuhin Competition, the Olympics of violin.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our designers are dressing Hollywood stars – Dzojchen’s suits are worn by Robert Downey Jr, Chadwick Boseman and Nick Jonas.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, when Ironman is not in his iron armour, he is in a Singapore suit!

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Heliopolis Accessories’ clutch bags have been worn by Emma Roberts and Janelle Monáe.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our sportsmen and women have done us proud.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Jason Chee, table tennis gold at the ASEAN Paralympic Games.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And we have scaled Everest – Dr Kumaran Rasappan and also Nur Yusina Ya’akob, the first Malay/Muslim woman from Singapore, to reach the world’s highest peak.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And we are not doing too badly in the fun stakes.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Zouk is among the top clubs in the world.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And The Manhattan Bar at the Regent Hotel is Asia’s No 1 for the second year running, not bad for a small little red dot that you can barely find on any world map.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And this is not even the full list of our achievements.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are more which I will mention later.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some of you may have felt slightly uncomfortable during my recitation of this long list of achievements.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If so, you are displaying another very Singaporean trait, which is modesty.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are not given to blowing our own trumpet or puffing ourselves up.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If anything, we are embarrassed by praise and accolades.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We tend to duck our heads and mumble something about just doing our duty.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But this is not about chest thumping or bragging.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is about understanding the significance of what I have just listed.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Those things could not have been achieved by any single person, organisation or the Government acting alone.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Those were achieved by the collective effort of Singaporeans, each contributing in different ways.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To have been able to achieve all those things despite the odds, despite our size, despite our lack of resources, tells you something about us.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We do not give up, not even when faced by seemingly insurmountable obstacles.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It tells you that we are resourceful and entrepreneurial.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are the kind of people who will create something out of nothing, based just on the power of an idea.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It tells you we are innovative, able to adapt, to break new ground.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If there is a worthy challenge, we will rise to the occasion and meet it.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We were once told that we were just a little red dot, a remark that was meant to put us in our place and remind us how small we are.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Instead, we took that label and we turned it into a badge of pride and a mark of excellence.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But being Singaporean is not just about achievements.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our achievements are the manifestation of something much deeper and more fundamental – care.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Above all, to be Singaporean is to care.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To be Singaporean is to care about family, about others, about country.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this debate, much has been said about social mobility, inequality and the lack of social mixing.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, in the context of identity, the real point to note is not that this is becoming a problem.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The real point to note is that we care that it is becoming a problem and we are determined to do something about it.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We care enough to want to do something.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If we see something wrong, our first instinct is to help, to fix it, to improve the situation.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We care about our children and their future.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We want every child to fulfil his or her fullest potential, to give every child the opportunity to succeed, irrespective of starting point.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And that is the reason why we put so much emphasis on education.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our students are also the world’s No 1 for problem solving through teamwork.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is PISA 2015’s Study on Collaborative Problem Solving.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And this includes progress made by academically weaker students.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is from Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS) 2015.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Again, I cite this data not for the sake of trumpet blowing, but to ask people to look at the story that this data tells you.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The data tells the story of how, over the years, our educators have built an exceptional education system where our students outperform their peers internationally.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This was and continues to be driven not by a desire to top the rankings but by the desire to ensure that our children succeed, and to give them the best chance to navigate the future and to help them be the best that they can be.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this regard, I was struck by what the former Director-General of Education Ms Ho Peng said in her speech at the Appreciation Dinner upon her retirement.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She said: "We never went out to be a world-class education system but, through good thinking, planning and sheer hard work, we woke up one day to the realisation that we were regarded as world-class.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The idea took some getting used to – and I hope never.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Because education is such a complex business, it is, after all, to mould the future of our nation, that we must never be complacent, to always keep on our toes, to be forward-looking and yet, remain connected with the ground, the voices of students, teachers, school leaders, parents and the community." That is how our educators see their mission.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Yes, there is anxiety about stress and competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is also a need to shift the focus from an over-emphasis on academics to embrace a broader skills approach.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have made several moves in the last few years, and we will do more.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But this, too, is an example of our Singaporeanness; we are never content to rest on our laurels.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We worry for those who may lose their jobs to technology.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We want our people to be fully employed.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We want them to be able to cope with change so that they can secure their livelihoods, and care is the driving impetus behind SkillsFuture and Adapt and Grow.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We care about whether our people have jobs.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, that is where we direct our efforts.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second among 190 economies for ease of doing business.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are top in Asia for best protection of intellectual property (IP).

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Again, what story do these survey results tell?

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is certainly not about growth for growth’s sake.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: What that data reflects is the enormous continuing effort that goes into trying to keep Singapore the best place to do business so that foreign investments will flow in, so that companies are anchored here, to make us a global exchange for goods and services.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For one purpose: to generate opportunities and jobs for our people so that we can make a better living.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are first in the world for life expectancy at birth, both sexes; first in the world for health-related sustainable development; second in the world for healthcare efficiency; and healthiest country in Asia and fourth in the world.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I am not sure how many other countries’ prime ministers tell you to eat brown rice!

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Again, this data speaks of our concern that our people should lead long and healthy lives.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is testament to the work that goes in to ensure that we are healthy and that, if for any reason we fall ill, Singaporeans can get the best possible healthcare.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The home ownership rate among resident households for Housing and Development Board flats is 92.1%.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the last decade, we have expanded our social networks, increased social programmes and increased social expenditure.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That includes the Pioneer Generation Package, the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), Silver Support, ComCare, MediShield Life, to name just a few – again, because we care.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This can be seen in many ways, for example, our response to the tsunami in 2004 and the Nepal earthquake in 2015.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Total volunteer hours have almost doubled from 66 million hours in 2014 to 121 million hours in 2016.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But our other Singaporean trait is that we are also pragmatic.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Care has to be deliverable and sustainable, both operationally and financially.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And that is the other part of our identity, too, that is, making sure that things actually get done.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We work hard to translate care into reality.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And that is why the Singapore Tourism Board tagline is "Passion made Possible", accompanied by the trust mark.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For us, it is not enough to get things done just for today.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are also a people who think about tomorrow, about the future of our children and the future of Singapore, our country.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Committee on the Future Economy and its work is about the future, as, indeed, is this debate.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our preoccupation with the future is driven by our sense of duty and stewardship, that we must not only tend to our own generation but plant seeds that will bear fruit for the next.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are green, we care about our environment and we love nature.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Long before the green movement, we had annual tree planting.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: From a Garden City, we have moved to being a City in a Garden.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our Botanical Gardens is a World Heritage Site.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have Gardens by the Bay, the upcoming Rainforest Park at Mandai.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are a Permanent Observer of the Artic Council.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And we have designated this year as the Year of Climate Action.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Just look at our response to the animals which share our urban home – otters, owls, woodpeckers.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Campus Creatures is a popular Facebook page on animals seen around our schools, junior colleges, polytechnics and universities.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Animal rescue and shelters are gaining more prominence.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Before we have finished one meal, we are discussing the next!

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have our traditional hawker food, but young Singaporeans are coming up with creative new concepts.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is traditional kong bak bao, but with innovative new fillings of salted egg yolk, chicken and prawn, chilli crab, crispy chicken with Japanese tartar sauce.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Windowsill Pies, set up by brothers Jonathan and Sean Gwee – yummalicious sweet pies.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is the Hainanese chicken rice and laksa potato chips by F.EAST, a Singapore husband and wife team – Lee Yue Jer and Kee Vern Cheng.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And salted egg yolk fishskin and chips from Golden Duck by Singaporean duo Jonathan Shen and Christopher Hwang.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In fact, we have taken to putting salted egg yolk on just about everything!

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is fast becoming part of the Singapore food scene.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And, for those who have not tried the Golden Duck’s fishskin and chips, I have arranged for Parliament to put some packets in the Members’ Room during the break.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Then, we have a uniquely Singaporean sense of humour.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Think Phua Chu Kang, the Noose and, more currently, the Ryan Sylvia YouTube Channel.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are champion complainers, although Ministers from other countries have assured me that we do not have a monopoly on this!

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And yes, we are kiasu; we are impatient.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But overall, our positive attributes far outweigh our negative ones.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But what makes us truly unique is our strong sense of unity.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore is exceptional not because everyone is a superstar.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If you ask Singaporeans, many will say they are just ordinary people doing ordinary things.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But we are exceptional – and we have achieved extraordinary things – because of our unity, the way in which we pull together.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: You must help to write the next chapter.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: You have the qualities, the values and the opportunity to do so.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To the students of Tembusu College, not all the answers are clear right now because the story is being written.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But you will be part of that story and you will write that story, together with the 4G leadership and with your fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: No matter what our background, each of us has a role to play.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Each has something to contribute to make Singapore a better place.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education, Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As in an orchestra, each instrument, taken alone, may not sound very musical.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam stands between us and tea break.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (In Malay):  : This year, President Halimah Yacob delivered her maiden President’s Address.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For me, it was a proud moment and a source of inspiration.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Seeing a Malay lady as the President delivering an address charting the direction of our country, made me really think about progress in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In Singapore, a woman can occupy the highest position in society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In Singapore, a minority race can have the same status as the other races.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In Singapore, if we are willing to work hard, there are pathways and opportunities to keep progressing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I admit, and I am aware, that not everyone has the same situation in life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For instance, a particular family’s financial situation and the lack of social networks and social capital, can definitely impact one’s direction in life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Those who come from low-income families generally need to work harder compared to those who come from wealthy families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This turns the pursuit of progress into an unfair competition.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This year’s President's Address has certainly outlined inequality as an issue that we must overcome.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am heartened to see the Government giving due attention to this issue and making it a national priority.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I recall when I was a student, and when there was an opportunity to take part in a study visit overseas, I did not even think about participating because I knew the cost was high and my parents could not afford it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Overseas programmes are not necessarily a priority, but such activities, which are done outside the classroom, are opportunities to gain new experiences and knowledge.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Each student should be able to grab any opportunity in the course of his or her education, regardless of background.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Many parents may be able to afford to provide more for their children.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The reason is that although parents from this group may be able to afford certain things for their children, the cost of living may affect their ability to provide additional things.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It will be good if support can also be rendered to these families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The Government may be able to implement certain policies and programmes but, in the end, all of us play a role in ensuring that our society can progress together.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We must make use of the available opportunities, provide support and assistance where possible, and work together to enhance the standard of living of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, allow me to continue in English.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Many of my esteemed colleagues in this House had shared their insights from their interactions and discussions with residents and other groups of people.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Allow me to add to this and share some of my insights.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For one, the people want an efficient Government, one that responds to issues quickly and solves all problems immediately.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The people I spoke to lamented about transportation woes, problems with shared bicycles, danger imposed by personal mobility devices.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Whilst they acknowledge the current efforts in place to resolve the issues, many hope for a faster solution.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some shared that the Government should not be high-handed in its approach in responding to criticism, and that there should be better acceptance of its inadequacies and a willingness to change and do better.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For some people, the many lofty plans and policies will not matter if at the end of the day it does not make their lives better.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The expectation on the Government is very high.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The previous generation of leaders set high standards of efficiency, of integrity and we should build on these standards.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, the challenge faced by the new generation of leaders is great.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Issues about maintaining or, in fact, earning and building trust have surfaced.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are vocal groups who may be in the minority, but their dissent is strong and their views are amplified through social media.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We all have confirmation biases and social media helps create echo chambers where already-held beliefs, no matter how unreasonable they may be, are reinforced.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is an uphill battle, but I have faith in the leadership.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am heartened by the candour and humility of the Government.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Over the last few days of this debate, I have heard the acknowledgement and acceptance of the people’s grievances, their feedback, and the plan and determination to do better.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I feel that it is this earnestness and courage that define this current Government.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: As Minister Indranee articulately put it just now, it is our values that define us, and I believe that our values will guide us through any turning points in our journey as we continue writing our Singapore Story.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think we all need a tea break now.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And just to show a little bit more care, I will take the Chair at 2.05 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 1.40 pm until 2.05 pm.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over these past five days, Members have shared their concerns and also their hopes for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
