text: Members of Parliament spoke about the immediate issues that Singaporeans are concerned with, such as jobs, cost of living, inequality.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I explained in this year's Budget some of the measures that we are taking to meet the immediate concerns of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members of Parliament also spoke about our longer-term challenges: geopolitical and economic shifts in our region and the world, technological advances and disruptions that will transform how we live and work, and new social divides that test our cohesion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must not only navigate the choppy waters that are immediately around us, but have a sense of where we are going, where we are headed towards.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When it comes to the longer-term challenges, we are taking action, we are working to secure opportunities for our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Each generation must forge its own way forward.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the Prime Minister put it, a Government must govern.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, I would like to share some thoughts on how we can take Singapore and Singaporeans into the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are two vital parts to this: how we continue bringing out the best in our people; and, how we continue building a culture of partnership and trust in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, how will we continue bringing out the best in our people?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the central question that should occupy each generation of leaders because Singaporeans are at the heart of everything this Government does.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This stays constant, whichever the generation of leadership: 1G, 2G, 3G, 4G or 10G.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: New circumstances call for new approaches from us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, each successive generation must ask anew: how do we bring out the best in our people?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How do we make life even better for our people?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans of all backgrounds enjoy a safe and secure environment, home ownership, world-class education and good job opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people lead fulfilling lives and age with dignity, with the assurance of good quality and affordable healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A child born in Singapore today has one of the best odds in the world of having a safe, healthy and fulfilling life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are at a more advanced stage of development now.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Can we do better to support our people?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Ng Chee Meng set out how we will better support vulnerable workers so that they can face change with confidence.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Lawrence Wong described our city of tomorrow, one that embraces the future and is more innovative, inclusive and resilient.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I first said, "Every School a Good School" in this House.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After I did, some Members of Parliament (MPs) said, "every hawker centre a good hawker centre" and "Every MP a good MP".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Every school a good school is about bringing out the best in every child.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is what our schools have been doing, recognising that every child is unique.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through a combination of hard and soft ways.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Resource each school well; fire up educators with a sense of mission and purpose; create diverse pathways and programmes that cater to the different interests and talents of our children.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Equally important is how we have built on one another's work, and this came through very clearly whenever I discuss with Education Ministers at that time with ministers around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In MOE, I was fortunate that past Ministers for Education, including Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean, Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam and Dr Ng Eng Hen in this House, passed to me and my team a strong foundation to build upon.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that Minister Ng Chee Meng, and now Minister Ong Ye Kung have continued to build on this.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are now taking this same aspiration beyond our schools to our whole economy and society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Chan Chun Sing spoke of Singapore Unlimited.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, this is how we can broaden opportunities for our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Bringing out the best in our people is not just about helping Singaporeans to make a good life, to make the grade or make a living.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is about supporting Singaporeans to make a good life and to make a difference.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For this reason, it is not only what we know or what we can do that matters.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is what we are made of, what we stand for, that counts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Indranee Rajah spoke on our values and how they define us as a people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are some values and instincts that are intrinsic to the Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we are to bring out the best in every Singaporean, we must stay true to these values.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our existing values of thrift, hard work, resourcefulness and resilience serve us well and we must uphold them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In a new world of greater change, we will need a new emphasis on our values and develop 21st century competencies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: From our founding, we have been open to goods, ideas and peoples from around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Going forward, we must also be open to change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And not only to the change that comes to us, but go out and actively engage with it, seek our place amidst the change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This means keeping a sense of adventure about new possibilities and having courage in the face of challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have always embraced our wealth of cultures, languages and religions, and turned this diversity into a strength.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Going forward, I hope we also treat the growing diversity of perspectives, causes and success pathways as our endowment to treasure and nurture.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Pioneers, in a spirit of self-determination, fought hard for us to be masters of our own destiny.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Going forward, we must stay united against new forces, new fault lines, that may divide us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must discern and guard against misinformation, stay aware of what is happening around the world, understand and defend what Singapore stands for.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And when we chart our way together, we must do so with a respect for the truth and a sense of responsibility to one another.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our goal is to spark Singaporeans' sense of wonder and curiosity when young.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will take time, but we must continue to persevere.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To be Singaporean must mean to have the opportunities and abilities to see, seize and seek more of life's possibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our goal must be to make this true for every Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That is how we will continue bringing out the best in our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Next, I would like to speak about building a culture of partnership and trust to keep Singapore a special place for all of us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore can have a place in the world only as long as we stand for something special, and only as long as we stand united.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can stand for something special if we draw together the most of everyone's diverse strengths, from across all parts of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we can only stand together if we have strong bonds of trust among us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Partnership and trust work together, nourish each other.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The more we partner one another, the better we understand one another, the more the trust will grow.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With more trust, we partner and work together more readily.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A unity of purpose grows out of our diversity of strengths, through partnership.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If there are divisions, these will be exploited.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: You see this in many parts of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we stand united, we stand tall among nations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this House, we have Government MPs, Opposition MPs, Nominated MPs and Non-Constituency MPs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We engage in vigorous debate, as we should.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But when it comes to the crunch, there must be no doubt about one thing: that every single one of us is totally committed to the long-term interests of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Whatever our views, let us come together to safeguard our sovereignty and serve the long-term interests of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: President Halimah has called for us to foster a deeper people-Government partnership.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This partnership must be sincere and grounded in trust, with all stakeholders playing meaningful and complementary roles.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Each generation of leaders has worked to strengthen the people-and-Government and people-to-people partnerships, building trust between the Government and the people and among all parts of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At critical junctures, we came together to chart our course for the future – The Next Lap in 1991, Singapore 21 in 1999, Remaking Singapore in 2002.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Prime Minister said that we need new ideas, new bonds and new connections in every generation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The public is interested in how the 4G political leadership is taking shape.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They recognise, rightly, that this is important for our country's future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To build new ideas, new bonds and new connections, we must also develop leadership in all parts of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our challenges become more complex, the Government will not have all the answers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to harness the diverse strengths of our society, through leaders at different levels in different parts of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By working together, we can achieve something greater than the sum of our parts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we must go beyond political leadership, to develop and embrace leadership in every part of society – from our unions and trade associations to NGOs and VWOs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we must be united by a sense of common purpose and galvanise whole-of-nation efforts to take Singapore forward.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Leadership in every part of society will define the quality of our partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is only when all parts step up, that we can best draw from diverse strengths across society to make a difference.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: My own interactions with leadership in all parts of society has been enriching and humbling.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Singapore Conversation and SG50 introduced me to leaders from many fields.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They care deeply about an issue or a group of people, take proactive steps to make things better.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More than that, they appreciate different points of view, engage in honest dialogue and work together with other groups.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Committee on the Future Economy and now the Future Economy Council are energised and strengthened by the contributions of leaders in business, unions and academia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Thomas Chua, Assoc Prof Randolph Tan and our Labour Members have been involved, and they can attest.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many private sector leaders are also working closely together with our political leaders in a number of focused committees to develop and act on this.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Just last week, I shared what we are working on with an eminent visitor from a very advanced economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When I described to him what we were doing with our ITMs, how we will bring in people together, he lamented that, "We are not even thinking about these issues, much less to bring people together".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And he ended up our discussion by saying, "This is why I am so impressed with Singapore and this is how you are going to stay successful".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, I think what we have achieved is not something to be taken for granted and that it is not the natural order of things.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to nurture this very carefully.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, in our discussions, businesses, unions, experts, they develop new products, new business models to take their sectors forward.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And with the experience they gained, they give back to the Future Economy process with ideas, feedback, even training programmes, to level up across the board.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Whenever I join our charities and VWOs for their events, I meet passionate leaders who are actively building a more caring and cohesive community, showing leadership.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, many Members of this House are serving your residents and Singapore in more ways than one, and through your own active philanthropic work – Ms Denise Phua at the Autism Resource Centre; Ms Rahayu Mahzam with the Malay Youth Literary Association; Ms Chia Yong Yong with the Society for the Physically Disabled; Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan with organisations in the legal field; and Mr Louis Ng at the Animal Concerns Research and Education Society (ACRES), and many other Members – it would not be possible to mention every one.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But this list shows how much all of you care.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More and more, I see different charity organisations coming together to do more together, and businesses are doing skills-based volunteering, lending their unique strengths to charities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All this to the benefit of the whole society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And all this is possible because every individual, each organisation, is able to develop to the best in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And this is something special and valuable that we must build upon.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am sure Members of this House all want to see more of such leadership in all parts of our society, and partnership among all parts of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will nurture this, even as we do our part to give support where it can make a difference, and to foster a stronger partnership between the Government and the people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: CNS is evolutionary in design but revolutionary in impact.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is an example of the kind of boldness that President Halimah has called for.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will be a big step forward in building a caring society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will be a big step, too, in building our Singapore culture of partnership and trust.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And partnership and trust extend beyond our shores.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to work closely together with our immediate neighbours, and strengthen our relations with ASEAN members and all our major partners.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These were very successful meetings that bring forward our partnership in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And I am very encouraged by our enthusiasm to find ways and means to cooperate and partner one another.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It augers well for the future of our region and for the future of Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members of the House have shared what we see are the key issues for our society in the years ahead, and what we would like to build for our future Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: You have raised important questions, issues and ideas, and we must take them beyond this Chamber.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore belongs to all Singaporeans, and we need a whole-of-Singapore effort to take this journey forward.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will partner Singaporeans each step of the way in our journey of building our future Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The 4G leadership will listen with humility and respect.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will consider all views with an open mind and adjust our course accordingly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will communicate the thinking behind our decisions clearly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will bring Singaporeans together and give everyone a role to turn ideas into concrete action.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will share our ideas and seek Singaporeans' views on them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In doing so, we capture the wider range of views and perspectives in our diverse society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will reach out to Singaporeans at different stages of life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Young Singaporeans are already coming forward through the ongoing Youth Conversations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Their views are important because they are our future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we want to hear from others like the Generation X, Baby Boomers and Pioneers, too.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will reach out to different segments of society – people in different occupations who have different interests and passions and who are contributing back to society in different ways.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will reach out to our workers through the unions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will reach out to our communities through the grassroots and Community Development Councils.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond these efforts, we want to reach out directly to volunteer groups, hobby groups and others who are actively contributing to society in their own ways.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through our discussions, we will share our ideas and seek your views.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will build trust and ambition for Singapore and foster a common purpose.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will galvanise action and partnerships across society towards our common goals.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In Mandarin):  : The building of our nation and homes are interconnected.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are able to build our homes and families only if the nation is strong.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In turn, the development of our nation is dependent on our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can only live and work in contentment and achieve happiness if our nation is prosperous and stable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The future of Singapore lies in the hands of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The younger generation, in particular, has the responsibility of creating new possibilities for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The rapidly changing external environment and new technologies bring challenges, but also opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will create the best conditions for Singaporeans to succeed, help them to seize opportunities, bring out the best in them, so that they can achieve their potential and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We believe that every profession produces top talents.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We hope that more successful people and leaders from different parts of society will come together to build our nation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also hope that Singaporeans can demonstrate the spirit of “One For All, All For One”, and strengthen social cohesion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In doing so, the partnership and trust between the Government and the people will deepen.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As long as Singaporeans stand united, both during good and tough times, and work together towards our common goal, we will build a better Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In English): The President has laid out the 4G leadership’s agenda for the coming years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can face the future well if we continue to bring out the best in our people, and if all of us pull together in this spirit of partnership.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have shared with the House our plans to engage Singaporeans in a series of discussions, and to give everyone a role to turn good ideas into actions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Come, let us unite in a new spirit.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has been decades since the National Anthem was composed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we sing these lyrics in a profoundly changed world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yet, the call has rung true across the generations and sounds just as clarion for ours.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our generation, unity is just as important as ever.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us unite in this new spirit of partnership and trust.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us strive together as one people, united in our values, undivided in our diversity, giving our best as one for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Over the past few days, 70 Members, including the Prime Minister, have passionately shared their vision and views, and actively debated on what is next for Singapore.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Members have covered several key themes around the President’s Address: a vibrant economy with equal job opportunities, social mobility and reducing inequality, building an inclusive society, visible leadership in building trust and strong partnerships between the Government and the people.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We acknowledge that Singapore is in an advanced stage of development.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: So, for the next 50 years, how can we do better as an economy, as a society, as one people and one nation?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With changing times, our future economy cannot simply be a measure of employment and gross domestic product growth.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Singapore’s early economic focus was on industrialisation and job creation.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Through an open economy and thriving on multilaterism, as Mr Vikram Nair said, we have made progress and continue to shift our focus to adapt to industry needs of the time.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We have since moved from mass manufacturing to high technology manufacturing; and now we are embarking on industry value-add and digitalisation.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Tripartism has played a significant role in our economy in the past decades.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Thanaletchimi have called for tripartism to help our workers to embark on the transformation journey at a faster pace and operationalise the ITMs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It is time to galvanise actions that create impactful initiatives on the ground.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We want quality and inclusive economic growth that can help provide jobs and help with the cost of living, as shared by Dr Tan Wu Meng and Mr Zainal Sapari.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We need to break new grounds, build new capabilities and transform vision into reality.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: New partnerships of public and private service model have to be forged.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Support has to be given to prevent unfair practices against small businesses.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This new world and its changes impact not only our citizens and businesses but also the regulators and the Government.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: They, too, need to adapt to social, political and global market dynamics.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Mr Patrick Tay, Mr Ang Hin Kee and Mr Desmond Choo urged the Government to study how the new models of technology like artificial intelligence will impact our workforce and the need for new legal framework around it.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Similarly, human resource support for freelancers and new models of contract workers that Mr Ang Hin Kee and I shared.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This calls for boldness in the way we do things.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Such bold shifts could mean a deviation from what we know best – the structured processes, well-trotted known sectors, MNCs and strict compliance.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: They further added that we need an effective trade mission, local trade associations and chambers to do more in implementing ITMs, to help our companies hunt better as a pack overseas and overcome the steep learning curve while venturing into foreign emerging markets.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For all these to work, it boils down to a key element in our economy – talent.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: To build a future workforce, we have to cultivate and attract talents.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat reinforced the importance of having labour laws that can ensure fair and inclusive employment practices to protect our local talents.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and Assoc Prof Randolph Tan suggested a differentiated intake approach of talents to help businesses, tap on technology to identify the future skills landscape and why the need for equality of opportunity through our industry transformation push.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: To cultivate such a workforce, it has to begin young and it starts from our education.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We must develop students with varied abilities, not just knowledge but applied learning and emotional quotient that make each individual holistic.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Such soft skills of empathy and character building are ever more critical as Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Miss Cheng Li Hui highlighted.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As the saying goes, "All roads lead to Rome".

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We should enable diversity in their learning process and broaden the definition of success.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Reward them for having learnt and not "mugged".

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Appreciate each child for their values and their demonstrable soft skills.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In the long run, such students would intrinsically have embraced the concept of lifelong learning and are always skillfully deployable in different fields.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Lifelong learning must also continue beyond tertiary education, as pointed out by Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Denise Phua.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With digitalisation and an immense economy outside Singapore, all talents – local and global – are not bounded by geography.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Minister Chan Chun Sing rightly pointed out that we need to have the skillsets and mindsets to compete internationally.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: There must be a balance to address the immediate and long-term needs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I see the key role of the Government in ensuring there is cross-cultural learning and knowledge transfer to gradually build our local talents over the long haul.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Not many economies in the world have evolved at our pace or are as well-organised as us.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: But having a good start is only the beginning.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Looking at the growth and rapid advancement of ASEAN countries and other economies like China, we cannot afford to rest on our laurels.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I hope we continue to sprint, to create and be a creative inventor or early adopter in the race, and not a follower.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: So, we must embrace emerging technology, turn them into useful innovations, and nurture new markets in our Smart Nation and beyond.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Instead, we should engender smart communities to support digital access programmes that can help the needy and vulnerable.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: To achieve all these, our economy needs to continuously create sufficient diversity and attractive jobs, provide work-life balance and develop a positive work culture to appeal to a young and dynamic workforce.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: After all, it takes a motivated and innovative society to produce outstanding results, as Mr Faisal Manap emphasised.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: So, let us continue to enlarge our economic pie to ensure there will be more opportunities for our people to pursue, and more outcomes for our people to share.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We must strive to do good together and further ensure we can reduce income inequality and enhance social mobility throughout all segments.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Our future city should be one that embraces diverse ideals and uplifts our fellow citizens from different backgrounds, a society where every generation has equal opportunities to achieve their dreams better than the previous generation.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Whilst finance, family conditions and job cycle vary for every individual, the duty of the Government is to ensure that every citizen has a place in the country, a home to live in, and every child grows up with equal access to education, jobs and a safe environment.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Meticulous planning, social strategies in place and precise execution are necessary.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Social cohesion in Singapore was brought about by many factors.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We need to continue to work on and strengthen the values that define us as a society.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Values of social good, what it takes to be an active citizen, how do we give and share with others – these are areas that we should promote, as noted by Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Dennis Tan, Mr Azmoon Ahmad, Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Chong Kee Hiong.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We need to get the basics of the society right and not discard what works just to be bold.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Only a good society with strong values and virtues can withstand the test of time.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This is a point that Mr Seah Kian Peng also referred to.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: A Tetris safety net is one weaved from layers of support, one that is expandable in scope and one that is fundamentally stronger when the layers fall in place.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It takes many hands to further ensure that no one is left behind.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I appreciate what Mr Louis Ng’s father has taught him, "There is beauty in giving than receiving." Many Members suggested, too, that we must encourage the spirit of community giving.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We are fortunate today that we have volunteers, social workers and civil society activists; people who have stood up for causes, listened to other people, gave back and helped others.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: But we will always have a need for more such helping hands in our society.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This explains why it is even more pertinent that we continue to work on options to cater for everyone.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: From education, healthcare, social networks, housing and integration policies, I hope that, with the additional resources in place, more people can benefit from the assistance available, more can express their individualism, achieve success of their own definition, and eventually pay it forward to help others along.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Third, we must strive to do more together as one people, one nation.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: There is much we want to achieve in the second term of this Government for our people, with our people.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: But we need to set our sights way beyond the current time, because nation-building is a journey with no end.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: A common thread amongst every theme that we touch upon as a Government is people.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As Minister Heng Swee Keat just said, people are at the heart and core of every policy and implementation that we do.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: How do we bring out the best in our people?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This is also a point that is made by Mr Alex Yam, Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In Singapore, people are and will always remain our most precious asset.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: They represent the talent, the essence of our society, and our hope for the future.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We are here to build a home, a home that brings happiness, warmth, developments and one that allows every elderly, especially the seniors ahead to age in a dignified way.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Family units remain as the bedrock of our society and is our first line of support.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: But the people in our community can make a difference to our lives, too.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: They can become the extended family – neighbours and volunteers who help other needy families, seniors, working mothers, families with few dependants.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This, in the words of Ms Joan Pereira, and also described by Minister Indranee Rajah, is the true kampung spirit we have – the care for the people around us.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Each action, each step, is a sign of strength, unity and hope to fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In all that we do, as a citizen, student, parent, caregiver, worker or employer, we must always bear in mind the goal of making this country a more inclusive one.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Mr Darryl David also added how we can provide education support for neuro-divergent students and one which I strongly support, too.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As we strive to do well as an economy and do good as a society, the process is just as important as the outcome, exactly what Ms Sun Xueling mentioned earlier.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I trust the Government will strive to constantly work and give of their best to Singaporeans.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As we have heard from Members in this House, leadership, teamwork, empathy and trust are very important characteristics to have in our 4G leaders.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The need to work together as a team, to listen with compassion and humility, open to alternative views, deepen engagement and build trust with the people was strongly echoed by Mr Christopher de Souza, Mr Pritam Singh, Mr Ganesh Rajaram, Mr Murali Pillai, Ms Chia Yong Yong and Mr Kok Heng Leun.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As citizens, we should also share our views and ideas, endeavour to work with the Government in the spirit of encouragement and experimentation for an optimum outcome each time.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We must create our future Singapore together, because Singapore belongs to all of us.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We can best succeed when we share this journey together.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I brought my parents to the Frances Yip concert last month.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Before the close of the concert, Frances introduced a Singaporean songwriter and music producer, Mr Eric Ng, on stage.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Eric went on to share his background and talked about his career and how he got into this industry.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In all his excitement, he told us that it really started because of a mentor who was willing to give him that first opportunity that truly, indeed, became his first big break into the music industry.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: He seized the moment and sincerely appealed to all in the audience.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This was what he said, “Most of you present here tonight, I believe, are Singaporeans.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For what I have been through, I know it would not have been possible without my teacher and a mentor who gave me the opportunity.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: So, here with me tonight, I have here my own mentees and potentials who will become big in this industry.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Thus, I am appealing to all of you to do the same and support local talents.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Give these talents a chance, because I know they will make their mark someday.” His appeal was a simple one, but it moved me.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Yes, actually many of us should really be doing this for our fellow Singaporeans, be it mentorship, guidance, giving and sharing our experiences and knowledge.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This is the spirit we want to have in Singapore.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We are able to build things together, look out for one another, not judging others by their backgrounds, but actually treating them with dignity and giving them a chance based on their merits.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In short, it is a place where we find anchors in a country that we are truly proud to call our home.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Before we proceed to the Second Reading, I would like to remind Members, while I appreciate the familiarity and camaraderie that all of you share, do refrain from addressing fellow Members by their first name.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, do address one another a bit more formally.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the day.
